Extract matches and capture groups

Source: R/capture.R
re_extract.Rd

re_extract() returns the first match in each element of x, or one of its groups; re_extract_all() returns every match. re_match() returns every group of the first match as a data frame with one row per element; re_match_all() returns one row per match. The strings are built in C, without the per-match R overhead of regmatches() or utils::strcapture().

Usage

re_extract(x, pattern, group = 0, limits = NULL)

re_extract_all(x, pattern, group = 0, n = Inf, limits = NULL)

re_match(x, pattern, proto = NULL, limits = NULL)

re_match_all(x, pattern, n = Inf, limits = NULL)

Arguments

x

A character vector, a raw vector, or a list of raw vectors. NA (or NULL in a list) gives NA.

pattern

A character vector or an re vector; see Patterns.

group

The group to extract: a number, 0 for the whole match, or a group name.

limits

A re_limits() object, or NULL for getOption("zuregex.limits") and then PCRE2's defaults.

n

The most matches to return per element, Inf for all.

proto

NULL for character columns, or a data frame or list with one element per group, as for utils::strcapture(): each column is converted with as.<class>() for the class of the matching element, and takes its name. S4 classes are not supported.

Value

re_extract(): a character vector, NA where there is no match. re_extract_all(): a list of character vectors, NA for an NA subject or pattern.

re_match(): a data frame with one row per subject and one column per group, all NA where there is no match. re_match_all(): a data frame with element and match columns, then one column per group, one row per match; a subject with no match has no rows, and an NA subject or pattern one row of NA.

Strings from character input are in UTF-8; from bytes they are marked as "bytes".

Groups and columns

Groups are numbered from 1; group 0 is the whole match. In re_match() a named group's column takes its name and an unnamed group's column its number, so (?<year>\\d+)-(\\d+) gives the columns year and 2. A group that did not take part in the match is NA.

With one pattern per element, the columns are the union of the patterns' groups in order of first appearance: groups with the same name share a column, unnamed groups share a column by position, and an element whose pattern lacks a group has NA there.

Patterns

pattern is a character vector of regular expressions, compiled through the cache with the default options, or an re vector from re_compile() for flags, dialects and literal patterns. It has length 1, used for every element of x, or exactly the length of x, pairing pattern[i] with x[i]. Any other length is an error: nothing is recycled. An NA pattern gives NA for its element.

Strings and bytes

Character input is matched as UTF-8; strings in other declared encodings are translated first. Invalid UTF-8 is an error of class zuregex_error_utf. A raw vector is one subject matched as bytes, as is each element of a list of raw vectors, and so is a character vector with any element marked as "bytes". Patterns are then compiled without UTF-8 support, so . matches one byte.

Examples

x <- c("2026-10-21", "1999-01-02 and 2000-03-04", "none", NA)
re_extract(x, "\\d{4}")
#> [1] "2026" "1999" NA     NA    
re_extract(x, "(?<year>\\d{4})-(\\d{2})", group = "year")
#> [1] "2026" "1999" NA     NA    
re_extract_all(x, "\\d{4}")
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "2026"
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] "1999" "2000"
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> character(0)
#> 
#> [[4]]
#> [1] NA
#> 

re_match(x, "(?<year>\\d{4})-(?<month>\\d{2})")
#>   year month
#> 1 2026    10
#> 2 1999    01
#> 3 <NA>  <NA>
#> 4 <NA>  <NA>
re_match(x, "(\\d{4})-(\\d{2})", proto = data.frame(year = 0L, month = 0L))
#>   year month
#> 1 2026    10
#> 2 1999     1
#> 3   NA    NA
#> 4   NA    NA
re_match_all(x, "(?<year>\\d{4})")
#>   element match year
#> 1       1     1 2026
#> 2       2     1 1999
#> 3       2     2 2000
#> 4       4    NA <NA>
